# Devin 2.0

By The Cognition Team2025.04.03

It's been a little over a year since we first shared Devin 1.0 with the world last March. Since then, we've been working hard to improve Devin based on your feedback.

Today, we're excited to announce Devin 2.0: a new agent-native IDE experience for working with Devin, along with a flexible new plan starting at $20.

Now you can:

*   **Spin up multiple parallel Devins**, each equipped with its own interactive, cloud-based IDE. This means you can easily multitask, tackling numerous tasks concurrently and stepping in to steer when needed.
*   **Collaborate with Devin.** Whether you prefer closely tracking Devin's progress or a more hands-off approach, Devin actively brings you in as needed, ensuring you’re always informed and in control.
*   **Review and edit Devin’s work.** Easily touch up changes, refine code, or run tests right within the Devin IDE itself, using familiar tools and shortcuts like Cmd+I and Cmd+K.

And, we're shipping three new features: Interactive Planning, Devin Search, and Devin Wiki.

### Interactive Planning

Scoping out a task in detail and clarifying what to do can often consume just as much time as actual execution in software development. With this in mind, Devin 2.0 proactively researches your codebase and develops a detailed plan.

Each time you start a session, Devin responds in seconds with relevant files, findings, and a preliminary plan. You can modify the plan to ensure that Devin's understanding of the task is aligned with what you have in mind, before letting Devin work autonomously.

### Devin Search

Understanding your codebase deeply is crucial before any complex work begins, yet it’s often a bottleneck in engineering workflows. We're introducing **Devin Search**, an agentic tool designed to explore and understand your codebases.

Devin Search enables you to ask questions directly about your codebase, and quickly get detailed answers with cited code. For more advanced queries that require extensive exploration, turn on **Deep Mode.**

### Devin Wiki

Devin now automatically indexes your repositories every couple hours, creating detailed wikis complete with comprehensive architecture diagrams, direct links to sources, documentation, and more.

### Hire Devin

You can start working with Devin 2.0 today at app.devin.ai.

For more information about [Devin Enterprise](https://devin.ai/enterprise), reach out to our Sales team [here](https://cognition.ai/get-started#company).

# Devin Pricing 2026: Free, Pro, Max, Teams and Enterprise

What each Devin plan costs after Cognition retired Core and Team, and who each plan fits.

### 🎯 Quick Answer: Devin Pricing in 2026

Devin has a free plan, **Pro at $20/month**, **Max at $200/month**, **Teams at $80/month plus $40/month per full dev seat**, and custom Enterprise pricing billed in Agent Compute Units (ACUs).

**Best for:** Developers choosing between a cheap editor-plus-agents plan (Pro) and heavier daily usage (Max).

## Devin plans at a glance

| Plan | Price | Highlights |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0  | Light quota, limited models, unlimited inline edits and Tab completions |
| Pro | $20/month | Higher quotas, frontier models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI, cloud agents, extra usage at API pricing |
| Max | $200/month | Everything in Pro with significantly higher quotas |
| Teams | $80/month plus $40/month per full dev seat | Up to 200 users, centralized billing, admin analytics, priority support |
| Enterprise | Custom | SAML/OIDC SSO, dedicated deployment option, dedicated account management; billed in ACUs |

## The 2-minute brief for AI builders.

## What changed from the old Core and Team plans

In April 2026 Cognition retired the old Core and Team plans, including the $500/month Team entry point. Self-serve plans now use included quota plus on-demand usage billed in dollars. Enterprise stays on ACUs. Old Core users moved to Free.

## What "Devin pricing" actually means now

Searching for Devin pricing used to lead to one number: the old Core plan or the $500/month Team plan, both billed in Agent Compute Units. That is no longer the case. Devin's pricing page now sells it as a coding environment with individual plans (Free, Pro, Max), a team plan, and an Enterprise tier you reach through a demo. The three questions people usually mean are: what does it cost to try, what does one developer pay, and what does a team pay. This guide answers each using the figures on Devin's own pricing page.

## Individual plans: Free, Pro and Max

Free costs $0 and includes a light quota to code with agents, limited model availability, unlimited inline edits and unlimited Tab completions. It is a real way to test the editor before paying, but the light quota and limited models mean it is not a daily driver for agent work.

Pro costs $20 per month. It adds increased quotas, access to frontier models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and SpaceXAI plus leading open-source models, full model availability, and access to cloud agents (Devin Cloud). Devin's page also lists free use of SWE-2 Free in Devin Desktop and the CLI through October 16, 2026, so that perk is time-limited. If you run out of included usage, you can buy extra usage at API pricing.

Max costs $200 per month and is labeled new. It includes everything in Pro with significantly higher quotas. Devin does not publish a specific number for how much higher, so treat Max as a purchase for people who consistently exhaust Pro, not as a plan you pick for features. The comparison table on the pricing page also lists higher concurrent-session limits on the upper tiers (up to 10 on the lower plans, unlimited on the top ones).

## Team plan and Enterprise

Teams is $80 per month for the team plan plus $40 per month for each full dev seat, for up to 200 users. Each full user gets their own quota and access to Devin Desktop. Team features include sharing and collaboration, centralized billing, an admin dashboard with analytics and priority support. A quick example: five developers cost $80 + 5 x $40 = $280 per month before any extra usage. Ten developers cost $480.

Enterprise is custom priced through a demo. Devin's page lists highest-priority support, dedicated account management, SAML/OIDC SSO, centralized admin controls, a dedicated deployment option, VPC deployment, and first-class support for every major model provider.

## How usage works and how to stretch it

Every paid plan includes a usage allowance that refreshes automatically on a daily and weekly basis. Devin says most users will not hit their limits, and that cost per message depends on the model, the size and complexity of the task, and the reasoning required. If you go past your allowance, extra usage is consumed at API pricing.

Devin's own advice for making limits last: keep prompts precise and strip unnecessary context, and switch to smaller models for routine work. It names Haiku, GPT 5.2 Mini and open-source models like Kimi K2.5 as examples that extend your usage. In practice, that means using a frontier model for hard multi-file tasks and a mini model for renames, small fixes and boilerplate.

## Pro vs Max vs Teams: which one fits

Solo developer trying agents: start on Free, move to Pro when the quota or model limits get in the way. Solo developer using agents all day: Pro first. Upgrade to Max only after you see yourself buying extra usage regularly, since extra usage on Pro is billed at API rates and Max is a flat $200. Group of two or more who want shared billing and an admin dashboard: Teams. Regulated company that needs SSO and a dedicated deployment: Enterprise.

## How Devin compares to other AI coding tools

Devin's $20 Pro tier sits in the same price band as most AI coding subscriptions, so the choice comes down to workflow. Devin pairs a desktop editor and CLI with cloud agents. If you prefer an editor-first workflow, read our Cursor pricing guide. If you want an agent that works from your terminal and repo, compare Codex pricing. For prompt-to-app builders aimed at non-developers, see Lovable pricing and Emergent pricing instead.

## Which plan should you pick?

Pro at $20 is the default for individuals who want cloud agents and frontier models. Move to Max only if you hit Pro quota regularly. Teams makes sense once several people need shared billing. Compare against [Cursor pricing](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/cursor-pricing) and [Codex pricing](https://www.nocode.mba/articles/codex-pricing) before you commit.

Devin now sells Free, Pro, Max and Teams plus Enterprise, after Cognition retired Core and Team. Self-serve billing mixes included quota with on-demand credits, so the subscription sets the baseline and heavy use draws extra credits. # Billing and Procurement

Copy pageCopy page

How usage measurement, billing, and procurement work for Devin federal customers and public sector agencies.

Copy pageCopy page

This documentation is for the federal deployments of Devin. [Back to Devin Docs](https://docs.devin.ai/get-started/devin-intro)

We offer both usage-based pricing for access to the Cognition platform and firm-fixed-price (FFP) contracts for delivering mission outcomes.

* * *

## 

[​

](https://docs.devin.ai/federal/usage-and-billing#usage)

Usage

This is for customers that want to procure access to the platform for their engineers and/or their mission partner engineers. Usage-based pricing is shared across all deployments and products on the Cognition platform. For example, you can seamlessly move between a commercial and federal deployment, or from Devin Cloud to Devin Desktop. Usage is measured in Agent Compute Units (ACUs), which represent how much actual work the agent is doing. The price of each ACU depends on the deployment level. For example, IL5 is more expensive than FedRAMP High. A more detailed breakdown of what contributes to usage can be found [here](https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/usage). Many customers have existing purchase agreements with CSPs like AWS, Azure, and Google. We do not want customers to pay twice for intelligence. Thus, customers are able to burn down their CSP commitments with their existing accounts through utilization of Devin.

## 

[​

](https://docs.devin.ai/federal/usage-and-billing#firm-fixed-price)

Firm-fixed-price

This is for customers that want to procure the completion and delivery of a mission outcome on firm-fixed-price basis, regardless of how much compute or labor is spent by Cognition. The combination of our platform, deployed engineers, and partnerships with federal solution providers, allows us to not only provide a developer tool, but to deliver mission outcomes faster, better, and cheaper than ever before. In each firm-fixed price contract, Cognition will provide a Scope of Work that specifies the mission outcome, SLAs, and hand-off terms. Cognition will also budget a number of ACUs and man-hours required to execute the scope of work. Following delivery, if there are any leftover ACUs, they will be credited back to the customer under regular usage-based-pricing terms.

## 

[​

](https://docs.devin.ai/federal/usage-and-billing#billing)

Billing

We offer a number of purchase options, ranging from marketplaces to contract vehicles like [NASA SEWP V](https://www.carahsoft.com/sewp) and [ITES-SW2](https://www.carahsoft.com/ites-sw2) through partners like Carahsoft. Please contact [public.sector@cognition.ai](mailto:public.sector@cognition.ai) to get started!
